summary: Investigating the performance and concurrency behavior of large transactions in PostgreSQL.
symptoms: Blocked transactions when two sessions attempt to update the same row.
Potential deadlocks or serialization errors depending on isolation levels.
mechanism: PostgreSQL's MVCC (Multiversion Concurrency Control) ensures that reads do not block writes and vice versa, but concurrent writes to the same rows can lead to blocking or errors.

value.concurrent_writes_to_same_row: blocked until the first transaction commits or rolls back

facts.evidence: User-provided example with two sessions attempting to update the same row.

value.read_committed: second transaction waits for the first to finish

assumptions: The database is configured with the default isolation level (Read Committed).
The table has appropriate indexes to support the update operation efficiently.
unknowns: The exact schema of the table being updated.
The distribution of data within the table.
The specific isolation level configured in the database.
